I'm applying for the Full-Stack Software Engineer role.

You're looking for someone who can write Rust, build full-stack systems, and work directly with customers. I've done all three—at the same time.

At Webflow, I built the Webflow Way Validator, a Designer Extension that checks templates against best practices. It validates design systems, components, styles, SEO, and accessibility. JavaScript was too slow for large projects, so I wrote the performance-critical parts in Rust and compiled to WASM. It runs 3x faster now. That's not a side project—it's in production, used by template creators every day.

I also built the App Submission Form (Next.js, PostgreSQL) and the Webflow Dashboard (SvelteKit, Cloudflare). These are the systems that power marketplace operations—handling retries, tracking submissions, managing assets with version history and rollback.

Before building systems, I spent years working directly with customers. I started in support, helping 500+ people get unstuck. I led a team. I moved to Education and helped launch Webflow University 2.0—creating content for everyone from beginners to developers. I learned how to explain complex technical concepts to different audiences.

SpruceID's forward-deployed engineering model—building alongside customers, translating requirements into production systems—is exactly how I work. The difference is the domain: identity and credentialing instead of web design. I don't have direct experience with Verifiable Credentials or DIDs, but I learn fast, and I understand why privacy-preserving identity matters.

I'm based in Texas, comfortable with remote work, and excited about mission-driven technology. I'd love to help state governments and public sector partners build better identity infrastructure.
